text: Proposition thirty-eight asks California to borrow eight
point four billion dollars for immunology and immunotherapy
research.
This funds research, not a guaranteed new treatment.
About half the money would go to one
qualifying research institute selected by the state.
The other half would support competitive grants through
a council of research institutions.
The analyst estimates five hundred to six hundred
million dollars a year in General Fund repayments
for about twenty years.
A voter might see long-term public research as
worth supporting even when returns are uncertain.
Another voter could object to the debt, the
concentration of funding in one institute, or committing
money before knowing results.
Yes authorizes this research borrowing; no rejects this
bond without
ending existing medical research.
